detailed.question: How do you access a USB disk connected to the router via network?
detailed.expected: By default all the network clients can access all folders on your USB disk. Refer to the following table for access instructions. You can also customize your sharing content and set a sharing account by referring to Customize Your Settings. Windows computer Method 1: Go to Computer > Network, then click the Network Server Name (ARCHER _D7 by default) in the Computer section. Note: Here takes Windows 7 as an example. Method 2: 1. Press Start ( )+ R on the keyboard (or select Start > Run) 2. Type the server address \\tplinkmodem.net or ftp://tplinkmodem.net in the dialog box 3. Click OKs Mac 1. Select Go > Connect to Server 2. Type the server address smb://tplinkmodem.net or ftp:// tplinkmodem.net 3. When prompted, select the Guest radio box 4. Click Connect Note: If you have set up a username and a password to deny anonymous access to the USB disks, you should select the Registered User radio box. To learn how to set up an account for the access, refer to To Set up Authentication for Data Security.
detailed.generated:
1. Connect your USB disk to the modem router's USB port directly or using a USB cable and wait for the USB LED to become solid on.

2. On a Windows computer, go to Computer > Network and click the Network Server Name (e.g., ARCHER_D7 by default) in the Computer section.

3. Alternatively, press Start + R, type \\tplinkmodem.net or ftp://tplinkmodem.net in the dialog box, and click OK.

4. On a Mac, select Go > Connect to Server, type smb://tplinkmodem.net or ftp://tplinkmodem.net, select the Guest radio box, and click Connect.

5. If authentication is set up, select the Registered User radio box and enter the username and password.

detailed.question: How do you set up parental controls on the router?

Click View Existing Devices, and select the device to be controlled. Or, enter the Device Name and MAC Address manually. 5. Click the icon to set the Internet Access Time. Select the restriction mode. 1 ) In Blacklist mode, the controlled devices cannot access any websites containing the specified keywords during the Internet Access Time period. 2 ) In Whitelist mode, the controlled devices can only access websites containing the specified keywords during the Internet Access Time period. 9. detailed.question: What should you do if you cannot access the router's web interface?
detailed.expected: Make sure the modem router connects to the computer correctly and the corresponding LED indicator(s) light up. Make sure the IP address of your computer is configured to obtain an IP address automatically and obtain DNS server address automatically. Make sure the default access you input is right.
detailed.generated:
The problem indicates that there is an issue with accessing the modem router's web management page.

1. Ensure the modem router is correctly connected to the computer and the corresponding LED indicators are lit.
2. Configure your computer to obtain an IP address and DNS server address automatically.
3. Verify that the default access URL you are using is correct.
4. Check and adjust your computer's network settings by navigating to Start > Control Panel > Network and Internet, and ensure the LAN settings are correctly configured.
5. Try using a different web browser or computer to log in.
6. If the issue persists, reset the modem router to factory default settings by holding the WPS/RESET button for 8 seconds, then attempt to log in again.

detailed.question: What are the possible causes if wireless devices cannot connect to the network?
detailed.expected: 1.	Authenticating problem, password mismatch. 1 ) Sometimes it will ask you to type in a PIN number when you connect to the wireless network for the first time. This PIN number is different from the Wireless Password/Network Security Key, usually you can only find it on the back of your wireless router/modem; 2 ) If you cannot find the PIN or PIN failed, you may choose “Connecting using a security key instead”, and then type in the Network Security Key/Wireless Password; 3 ) If it continues on saying network security key mismatch, it is suggested to confirm the wireless password on your wireless router/modem; Note: Wireless password/Network Security Key is case sensitive. 4 ) Connect to wireless network.
detailed.generated:
The problem indicates that there may be issues with network authentication, signal strength, or configuration settings. 

1. Ensure the correct Network Security Key/Wireless Password is entered, as it is case-sensitive.
2. Check the wireless signal strength; if weak, move the router closer to the device.
3. Change the wireless channel of the router to 1, 6, or 11 to reduce interference.

detailed.question: What is the purpose of IP & MAC Binding feature?
detailed.expected: IP & MAC Binding, namely, ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) Binding, is used to bind network device’s IP address to its MAC address. This will prevent ARP spoofing and other ARP attacks by denying network access to an device with matching IP address in the Binding list, but unrecognized MAC address.
detailed.generated: The purpose of the IP & MAC Binding feature is to prevent ARP spoofing and other ARP attacks by binding a network device's IP address to its MAC address, thereby denying network access to a device with a matching IP address in the Binding list but an unrecognized MAC address.

detailed.question: What is Access Control and how does it differ from MAC Filtering?
detailed.expected: Access Control is used to block or allow specific client devices to access your network (via wired or wireless) based on a list of blocked devices (Blacklist) or a list of allowed devices (Whitelist). MAC Filtering exploits the uniqueness of the MAC (Medium Access Control) address, a unique 12-digit hexadecimal address (for example, D8:5D:4C:B4:46:EA) of every network device, to determine if the device can or cannot access your wireless network.
detailed.generated: Access Control is used to block or allow specific client devices to access your network (via wired or wireless) based on a list of blocked devices (Blacklist) or a list of allowed devices (Whitelist), while MAC Filtering uses the unique MAC address of network devices to determine if a device can or cannot access your wireless network.

detailed.question: How can you remotely access USB storage connected to the router?
detailed.expected: You can access your USB disk outside the local area network. For example: Share photos and other large files with your friends without logging in to (and paying for) a photo-sharing site or email system. Get a safe backup for the materials for a presentation. Remove the files on your camera’s memory card from time to time during the journey. Note: If your ISP assigns a private WAN IP address (such as 192.168.x.x or 10.x.x.x), you cannot use this feature because private addresses are not routed on the Internet. Now different clients with Internet connection can access the USB disk: Computer • To download, open a web browser and type the server address ftp://<WAN IP address of the modem router>:<port number> (such as ftp:// 59.40.2.243:21) or ftp://<domain name of the modem router>:<port number> (such as ftp:// MyDomainName:21) in the address bar, then press Enter on the keyboard. • To upload, use a third-party app for network files management. Pad • Use a third-party app for network files management.
detailed.generated:
To remotely access USB storage connected to the router, follow these steps:

1. Connect your USB storage device to the modem router's USB port and wait for the USB LED to become solid.
2. Visit http://tplinkmodem.net and log in with the password you set for the modem router.
3. Select Advanced > USB Settings > Sharing Access.
4. Ensure that the FTP server is enabled for remote access.
5. Use the router's WAN IP address to access the USB storage from outside the local network. Note: If your ISP assigns a private WAN IP address, remote access may not be possible.
